profile.shortBio: Dr. Ananya Mehra is a fictional medical educator and professor of physiology dedicated to making complex medical concepts accessible through engaging lectures, research and academic publications.
fullBio: Dr. Ananya Mehra is an academic medical educator with over 16 years of experience in physiology education, curriculum development and medical research.
Her academic interests include cardiovascular physiology, neurophysiology, clinical reasoning and innovative approaches to undergraduate medical education.
Through structured classroom teaching, visual learning resources and digital lectures, she works to connect fundamental scientific principles with practical clinical understanding.
Her academic contributions include authored textbooks, research publications, conference presentations and mentoring medical students.
profile.personalStatement: The true purpose of education is not simply to share knowledge, but to inspire the curiosity to discover more.
profile.mission: To make medical education accessible, concept-driven and relevant to real-world healthcare.
profile.vision: To inspire a generation of healthcare professionals who combine scientific knowledge with curiosity, critical thinking and compassion.

faq.question: Where can I find the educational lectures?
faq.answer: Explore the Teaching section for organized physiology lecture series and individual video resources.

faq.question: Are the lectures free to access?
faq.answer: The prototype represents publicly accessible educational lecture collections. Actual video availability will depend on the final YouTube links.

faq.question: How can I inquire about books?
faq.answer: Use the Contact section and select Books / Publications as your inquiry category.

faq.question: Can academic institutions request guest lectures?
faq.answer: Yes. Select Academic Collaboration in the inquiry form to send a professional request.

faq.question: Can I contact the doctor for medical emergencies?
faq.answer: No. This website's inquiry form is not intended for emergencies, patient records or personal medical consultations.
